findings: An infiltrative pancreatic cancer measuring 21 mm is observed in the body of the pancreas. Retropancreatic tissue invasion is noted. There is contact of more than 180° with the superior mesenteric vein, suggesting invasion. The tumor extends beyond the inferior border of the duodenum. No other local invasion factors are identified. Lymph node metastases are observed in three nodes at station 8p and one node at station 18. No other metastases are observed.

responses.content:
Task 1: Diagnose the local invasion factors of pancreatic cancer.

CH0 (no invasion of the common hepatic artery)
DU1 (invasion of the duodenum)
S0 (no invasion of the superior mesenteric vein)
RP1 (invasion of the retropancreatic tissue)
PV0 (no invasion of the portal vein)
A0 (no invasion of the abdominal aorta)
PL0 (no invasion of the pancreatic lymphatic vessels)
OO1 (invasion of the inferior border of the duodenum)

Task 2: Determine the classification for local invasion (T classification) of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the size of the tumor (21 mm) and the extent of local invasion, the T classification is T3.

Task 3: Determine the N classification of pancreatic cancer.

Regional lymph nodes for pancreatic cancer in the body of the pancreas are:
- Station 8p (left gastric artery)
- Station 12p (common hepatic artery)
- Station 17p (splenic artery)
- Station 18p (celiac artery)
- Station 8a (left gastric artery)
- Station 12a (common hepatic artery)
- Station 17a (splenic artery)
- Station 18a (celiac artery)

The patient's metastatic lymph node stations are:
- Station 8p (left gastric artery)
- Station 18 (celiac artery)

These are regional lymph nodes. Counting only the metastatic lymph nodes within the regional stations, there are 4 metastatic lymph nodes.

N classification: N1b

Task 4: Determine the M classification of pancreatic cancer.

There are no distant metastases observed, so the M classification is M0.

Task 5: Determine the resectability classification of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the results of Task 1 and Task 4, the tumor is not unresectable due to local invasion or distant metastasis. Therefore, the resectability classification is Resectable (R).

Task 6: Determine the overall stage according to the JPS staging system.

Based on the determined T (T3), N (N1b), and M (M0) categories, the overall stage is Stage IIB.
